pr_title: ansible-galaxy - set the cache file after getting all collection versions
pr_body:
##### SUMMARY
Manage the in-memory cache in _call_galaxy but let the caller set the file cache after getting paginated results.

Fixes #73071

##### ISSUE TYPE
- Bugfix Pull Request

##### COMPONENT NAME
lib/ansible/galaxy/api.py
pr_comments: Thanks for fixing this, kept on slipping my mind.

I guess this is probably a problem on Galaxy's side, but in case it is not, I'm creating this issue in ansible/ansible.

~~Random guess (since I saw more read timeouts today): could this happen if there is a read timeout while reading a later page, i.e. in that case the code eats the error and simply returns the truncated list?~~ Doesn't seem to be the case since I also saw timeout errors for URLs with page > 1.

I saw the bot set affects to 2.11, but I believe this is affecting any Galaxy download. I started seeing timeouts today too on 2.10.4 where nothing changed on our end. Is there something going on with Galaxy perhaps?

@Quantas the timeouts are unfortunately nothing new (ansible/galaxy#2302). There seem to have been more of them during the last days though (was mentioned by different people on IRC).

The CIs of the collections I'm working on use a basic retry logic as a workaround (try up to three times if it fails). Definitely not perfect, but at least most contributors don't get annoyed by the timeouts anymore.

This seems to be caused by #71904: when the first install errors out because of a timeout while fetching the version list, the incomplete version list is stored in the cache, and subsequent install calls directly use the cached incomplete version list and fail with this error.

CC @jborean93
